title: Transdiagnostic uni- and multimodal sensory processing
summary: Sensory processing, i.e. the reception and processing of sensory stimuli, is distinctive in many psychiatric diagnoses, such as autism spectrum disorders (ASD), schizophrenia, anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorders, depression and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). These abnormalities are often recognizable in hypersensitive or hyposensitive reactions to sensory stimuli, which can have a major impact on the daily life and well-being of those affected. There are so called transdiagnostic similarities across the various diagnoses. The aim of this study is to find out which transdiagnostic similarities and differences exist in sensory processing compared to healthy controls without a psychiatric diagnosis.  This could deepen our understanding of the emergence and development of mental disorders and inspire new therapeutic approaches.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult inpatients who agree to participate in the study with one of 6 diagnoses: 
F20.0 - F20.9 (schizophrenia)
F32.0 - F32.9 (depressive disorders)
F41.0 - F41.9 (anxiety disorders) 
F42.0 - F42.9 (obsessive-compulsive disorders) 
F84.0 - F84.9 (autism spectrum disorders)
F90.0 - F90.9 (hyperkinetic disorders)

Healthy controls
Exclusion criteria:
History of neurological disorders (e.g. seizures, stroke, multiple  sclerosis, dementia, head trauma), history of serious medical disorders (e.g. cancer, autoimmune diseases,
chronic inflammatory diseases, cardiovascular diseases) and Verbal IQ < 80

Healthy controls: no current or past psychiatric disorder, no current or past substance abuse
